title: Normalized multiplication of support quotient sheaves on products
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. Use ordinary sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf $A_T$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], on small representatives of the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Derived categories are unbounded localizations at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme] and a closed immersion $a:C\hookrightarrow T$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], write $j:T\setminus C\hookrightarrow T$ for its open complement and set
$$Q^\tau_{T,C}=\operatorname{coker}(j_!\underline A_{T\setminus C}\longrightarrow\underline A_T),\qquad \tau=\mathrm{et},\mathrm{proet},$$
where the arrow is induced by inclusion of the open object into the final object and extension by zero is [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero, def-weil-extension-by-zero]. Denote the quotient map by $r^\tau_{T,C}$. Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $Z\hookrightarrow X$, $W\hookrightarrow Y$ be closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Put $P=X\times_kY$, $S=Z\times_kW$, with projections $p_X,p_Y$ [def-pc-base-change]. In each topology multiplication of quotient generators specifies an isomorphism
$$e_\tau:p_X^*Q^\tau_{X,Z}\otimes_A p_Y^*Q^\tau_{Y,W}\xrightarrow{\sim}Q^\tau_{P,S},\qquad \overline a\otimes\overline b\longmapsto\overline{ab}.$$
Here tensor is the sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and pullback uses the constant coefficient inverse images [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. The same map is an isomorphism for derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor, def-weil-derived-tensor]. The maps $e_\tau$ are natural for maps of the two pairs of schemes and closed supports inducing the pullbacks in this formula.

source.place: Proof paragraph 4: multiplication of quotient generators identifies the product support quotient, with the etale and pro-etale normalizations.

proof.text: Work first on the etale site of $P$. The fibre product $P\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is of finite type as a base change followed by a composite of finite-type morphisms [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change], and $S=Z\times_kW\to X\times_kY=P$ is a closed immersion [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-products], so $Q_{P,S}$ is defined. Since $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian, $X,Y,P$ are Noetherian schemes [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. For $T=X,Y,P$ with support $C=Z,W,S$ and any affine open $V\subseteq T$, the preimage $V\setminus C$ under $j$ is an open subscheme of the Noetherian scheme $V$, hence Noetherian and in particular quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]; so each open complement $j$ is quasi-compact in the sense of [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], as required by the current quotient-flat statement. Abbreviate $F=p_X^*Q^{\mathrm{et}}_{X,Z}$, $G=p_Y^*Q^{\mathrm{et}}_{Y,W}$ and $H=Q^{\mathrm{et}}_{P,S}$. The coefficient-preserving exact pullbacks give quotient epimorphisms $q_X:A_P\twoheadrightarrow F$ and $q_Y:A_P\twoheadrightarrow G$; write $r:A_P\twoheadrightarrow H$. Put $I=\ker q_X$ and $J=\ker q_Y$. For a geometric point $\bar p$ of $P$, put $\bar x=p_X\bar p$ and $\bar y=p_Y\bar p$. The inverse-image stalk comparison and the quotient-flat lemma identify $F_{\bar p}$ with $A$ if $\bar x\in Z$, and with zero otherwise; likewise $G_{\bar p}$ is $A$ on $p_Y^{-1}W$ and zero elsewhere. These identifications send the germs of $q_X(a),q_Y(b)$ to $a,b$ on their supports. The stalk of $H$ is $A$ on $S$ and zero elsewhere, with $r(a)$ mapping to $a$. Stalk exactness identifies $I_{\bar p},J_{\bar p}$ with the kernels of these quotient maps. Finally $S=p_X^{-1}Z\cap p_Y^{-1}W$: a geometric-point map to $P$ factors through $Z\times_kW$ exactly when its two projections factor through $Z,W$, by the fibre-product universal property.

source.place: Tags 03Q1 (lemma-stalk-pullback) and 03PT (lemma-stalk-exact); quotient stalk input is lem-pur-support-quotient-flat

proof.text: The quasi-compact-complement check from step 1 applies to $X,Z$ and $Y,W$. In either topology each of the two pulled-back quotient sheaves is flat: apply the quotient-flat lemma on $X,Y$ and then flatness under ringed-topos pullback to $p_X,p_Y$. There is no extra flatness hypothesis on these projections or on $A$. Their degree-zero complexes are K-flat directly from the definition: for an acyclic complex $C$, the short exact sequences $0\to Z^nC\to C^n\to Z^{n+1}C\to0$ stay exact after tensoring with a flat sheaf $B$, so $C\otimes B[0]$ is acyclic. Thus the very degree-zero complexes $F[0],G[0]$ (and their pro-etale counterparts) can be used as K-flat representatives.

source.place: Tag 05VD (lemma-pullback-flat), Tag 03ER (definition-flat); K-flat verification from Definition 06YN

proof.text: The composite $I\hookrightarrow A_P\xrightarrow r H$ is zero. Indeed at $\bar p\in S$ its source is zero because $(q_X)_{\bar p}:A\to A$ is the identity, and at $\bar p\notin S$ its target is zero. To justify detection of a zero morphism here and below, take its image sheaf: exactness of stalks makes every image stalk zero, and stalk conservativity applied to $0\to\operatorname{im}$ makes that image sheaf zero. Consequently the cokernel property of $q_X$ gives a unique $A_P$-linear map $t:F\to H$ satisfying $tq_X=r$.

Use the action unitor $F\otimes_{A_P}A_P\cong F$, $x\otimes a\mapsto ax$, and compose with $t$. The unitor and its inverse $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ follow immediately from the balanced-tensor relations and sheafification in the definition of sheaf tensor. The composite $F\otimes J\to F\otimes A_P\to H$ vanishes: on $S$, $J_{\bar p}=0$ by step 1, so its source stalk is zero by the etale tensor-stalk lemma; off $S$, its target stalk is zero. Step 3's image argument detects its vanishing. The sheaf tensor here is over $A_P$, while the etale tensor-stalk lemma tensors over the ring $A$; these agree: by [lem-weil-pbc-constant-module-locally-constant] a section of $A_P$ over $U$ is a locally constant function $|U|\to A$, so locally it is a constant $a\in A$, and after sheafification the $A$-balancing relations already impose all $A_P(U)$-balancing relations, and conversely. Hence the stalk formula of that lemma applies to $\otimes_{A_P}$ and is used in this form here and in step 5. Since $F$ is flat, tensoring $0\to J\to A_P\xrightarrow{q_Y}G\to0$ gives an exact sequence ending in $F\otimes A_P\twoheadrightarrow F\otimes G$. Cokernel factorization therefore gives $e_{\mathrm{et}}:F\otimes G\to H$. Its defining equation is $e_{\mathrm{et}}(q_X(a)\otimes q_Y(b))=r(ab)$. This also uniquely characterizes it: $A_P\otimes A_P\to F\otimes A_P\to F\otimes G$ is epic, the first map being $q_X$ under the action unitors and the second epic by flatness of $F$.

source.place: Definition 03ER (definition-flat); tensor definition and etale geometric tensor stalk comparison (Tags 008B, 03EL)

proof.text: The etale tensor-stalk comparison, applied to $\otimes_{A_P}$ through the constant-scalar identification of step 4 [lem-weil-pbc-constant-module-locally-constant], identifies $(F\otimes G)_{\bar p}$ with $F_{\bar p}\otimes_A G_{\bar p}$ and carries the germs of pure tensors to tensors of germs. At a point of $S$, the morphism constructed in step 4 is $A\otimes_A A\to A$, $a\otimes b\mapsto ab$. Its inverse is $c\mapsto c\otimes1$, since $a\otimes b=ab\otimes1$. At a point outside $S$, at least one of $F_{\bar p},G_{\bar p}$ is zero, and $H_{\bar p}=0$, so the morphism is the unique isomorphism $0\to0$. Conservativity of etale geometric stalks now proves that $e_{\mathrm{et}}$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Theorem 03PU (theorem-exactness-stalks), with tensor stalks as in Tags 008B and 03EL

proof.text:
Apply $
u_P^*$ to $e_{\mathrm{et}}$. The exact comparison pullback identifies the constant ring with $A_P$ on the pro-etale site. The normalized comparisons in the quotient-flat lemma identify $
u_T^*Q^{\mathrm{et}}_{T,C}$ with $Q^{\mathrm{proet}}_{T,C}$, carrying the quotient maps to the quotient maps, for $T=X,Y,P$. The comparison-pullback lemma for $p_X,p_Y$ identifies $
u_P^*F,
u_P^*G$ with the two required pro-etale pullbacks. Use the ringed-topos cochain tensor comparison in degree zero to identify $
u_P^*(F\otimes G)$ with $
u_P^*F\otimes
u_P^*G$. Its explicit pure-tensor formula and compatibility with the action unitors show that the transported map sends $\overline a\otimes\overline b$ to $\overline{ab}$. Call this map $e_{\mathrm{proet}}$; it is an isomorphism because it is obtained from an isomorphism by a functor and isomorphism conjugations. Its normalization determines it uniquely: exactness of $
u_P^*$ preserves the epic generator map in step 4, and all the displayed comparisons carry that map to the pro-etale generator map. No detection of pro-etale isomorphisms by ordinary geometric stalks is used.

source.place: Final paragraph: tensor and the support product are transported to the pro-etale site; normalized tensor input is Stacks Tags 03EL and 07A4

proof.text: By step 2, in either topology the factors of the source are flat and their complexes concentrated in degree zero are K-flat. The K-flat derived-tensor construction therefore identifies their derived tensor with their ordinary tensor in degree zero. Under that identification use $e_\tau[0]$. This is the same multiplication map, and is an isomorphism in the unbounded derived category. The natural comparisons of the K-flat construction ensure that the identification used here is natural; there is no Tor-amplitude or boundedness assumption left to establish for these degree-zero K-flat representatives.

source.place: Tags 06YT and 06YU (definition-derived-tor); computation on K-flat representatives

proof.text: For naturality, let $f:X'\to X$, $g:Y'\to Y$ carry closed supports $Z'\subseteq X'$, $W'\subseteq Y'$ into $Z,W$ and put $h=f\times g$. In the etale topology the canonical maps $f^*Q_{X,Z}\to Q_{X',Z'}$, and likewise for $g,h$, are induced by the quotient maps of $A$: the kernel of $A\twoheadrightarrow f^*Q_{X,Z}$ maps to zero in $Q_{X',Z'}$. On $Z'$ the kernel stalk is zero because its image is in $Z$, and off $Z'$ the target stalk is zero; exact pullback, the quotient stalk formula and step 3 justify the factorization. For Cartesian supports these maps are isomorphisms by the same stalk test. Insert the inverse-image composition identifications and the tensor pullback comparison. Both composites in the naturality square for $e_{\mathrm{et}}$ send the generator $a\otimes b$ to the quotient class of $ab$: the tensor comparison respects action unitors, and the quotient maps preserve the images of $a,b$. The epic generator map of step 4, preserved by exact etale pullback, proves equality of the two composites. For pro-etale sheaves apply $\nu^*$ to this equality and use comparison-pullback naturality, the normalized quotient comparisons and the cochain tensor comparison with its composition coherence. This gives the identical square for $e_{\mathrm{proet}}$. Finally step 7 realizes the derived maps on these degree-zero complexes, so their naturality is the same equality of chain maps.

source.place: Tags 03D8 (lemma-push-pull-composition-modules) and 03EL; quotient naturality by cokernel uniqueness
